'''Paul Louis Riebesell''' (9 June 1883, [[Hamburg]] – 16 March 1950, Hamburg) was a German mathematician, statistician, actuary, and president of Hamburger Feuerkasse.<ref name=Vierhaus>{{cite book|editor=Vierhaus, Rudolf|title=Deutsche biographische Enzyklopädie: Poethen - Schlüter|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fGXU6_Wqg60C&pg=PA388|date=3 May 2011|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|isbn=978-3-11-094025-1|page=388}}</ref> At the [[w:International Congress of Mathematicians|International Congress of Mathematicians]], he was an invited speaker in 1932 in Zürich and in 1936 in Oslo.<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers}}</ref>

==Biography==
Riebesell studied mathematics and natural sciences at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]], at the [[Friedrich Wilhelm University of Berlin]], and at [[Kiel University]], where he received his doctorate in 1905 under the supervision of [[Paul Stäckel]]. After receiving his doctorate, Riebesell was a [[Studienrat (Germany)|''Studienrat'']] for a number of years at the [[University of Hamburg]]. In 1918, he became the second director of the Hamburg [[Jugendamt]].<ref name=NDB>{{NDB|21|559|559|Riebesell, Paul|Peter Koch|116532467}}</ref> He wrote a commentary on the ''Reichsgesetz für Jugendwohlfahrt'' (Youth Welfare Law). He published research on Einstein's theory of relativity. After he habilitated at the University of Hamburg, there at the beginning of the 1920s he was appointed an ''außerordentlicher Professor'' (non-tenured professor) in actuarial mathematics and remained in that position until 1934. In 1923, the city of Hamburg appointed him director of Hamburger Feuerkasse. In 1934, he was elected president of the ''Reichsverband des öffentlich-rechtlichen Versicherung'' (Reich Association of Public Insurance Companies). In 1937, he lost this position for political reasons. In 1938, he became the director of the life insurance company ''Isar Lebensversicherungs-AG'' with headquarters in Munich. He was also a [[Academic ranks in Germany|professor honorarius]] from 1935 to 1940 at the [[Technische Hochschule Berlin]] (TH Berlin), from 1935 at the [[ University of Berlin]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://x0b.de/Dozenten/ |title=Dozenten an der Berliner Universität |access-date=2020-06-28 |archive-date=2012-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120723014249/http://www.x0b.de/Dozenten/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and from 1938 at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]]. After WW II, he returned to Hamburg as president of Hamburger Feuerkasse and held that position until his death in 1950. In 1948, he co-founded the ''Deutsche Gesellschaft für Versicherungsmathematik'' (German Society for Actuarial Mathematics) and became its first chairman.

Riebesell dealt with the influence of currency devaluation on insurance benefits. His achievement in actuarial science lies primarily in the transfer of actuarial approaches from life insurance to [[property insurance]]. He published, with Rudolf Lencer, the textbook and reference book "Deutsche Versicherungswirtschaft" (6 vols., 1936–39).<ref name=NDB/>

During WWI, a thousand copies of Riebesell's booklet ''Mathematik im Krieg'' (Mathematics in war) were sent, free of charge, to the front.<ref>{{cite book|author=Aubin, David|author2=Goldstein, Catherine|author2-link=Catherine Goldstein|chapter=Placing World War I in the History of Mathematics|title=The war of guns and mathematics. Mathematical practices and communities in France and its western allies around World War I|editor=Aubin, D.|editor2=Goldstein, C.|location=Providence, Rhode Island|publisher=American Mathematical Society|pages=1–55|year=2014}} [https://hal.sorbonne-universite.fr/hal-00830121v1/document hal.sorbonne-universite.fr preprint]</ref>

Riebesell was a member of the [[NSDAP]].<ref>[https://litten.de/fulltext/cara.htm Freddy Litten: Die Carathéodory-Nachfolge in München 1938–1944]</ref> He signed the [[Vow of allegiance of the Professors of the German Universities and High-Schools to Adolf Hitler and the National Socialistic State|''Bekenntnis der Professoren an den Universitäten und Hochschulen zu Adolf Hitler und dem nationalsozialistischen Staat'']], which was published in November 1933.

In 1922, he married Elisabeth Lengstorf (1897–1976). They had two sons and four daughters.<ref name=NDB/>

* [https://books.google.com/books?id=KWfXAAAAMAAJ ''Die mathematischen Grundlagen der Variations- und Vererbungslehre''] (1916)<ref name="Dresden1918">{{cite journal|last1=Dresden|first1=Arnold|author-link=Arnold Dresden|title=Book Review: ''Die mathematischen Grundlagen der Variations- und Vererbungslehre'' von P. * ''Mathematische Statistik und Biometrik'' (1932 & 1944)
* ''Mathematik des täglichen Lebens'' (1942, banned after 1945 in the Soviet Occupation Zone,<ref>[http://www.polunbi.de/bibliothek/1947-nslit-q.html Polunbi Nr. 3338]</ref> & 1948)
* as co-editor: ''Handbuch der Versicherung'' (Hamburg 1938)
* ''Einführung in die Sachversicherungsmathematik'' (1936)
* ''Die Relativitätstheorie im Unterricht'' (1926)
* [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=uc1.$b416795&view=1up&seq=680&q1=riebesell ''Über die geometrischen Deutungen der Relativitätstheorie''], Mitteilungen der mathematischen Gesellschaft 5 (1914), pp.&nbsp;130–140.
* [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015000428790&view=1up&seq=135 ''Die Beweise für Relativitätstheorie''], Naturwissenschaften 4 (1916), pp.&nbsp;97–101. {{doi|10.1007/BF01509402}}
* {{cite journal|title=Die neueren Ergebnisse der theoretischen Physik und ihre Beziehungen zur Mathematik|journal=Die Naturwissenschaften|volume=6|issue=6|year=1918|pages=61–65|issn=0028-1042|doi=10.1007/BF01506400|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015000428337&view=1up&seq=97&q1=riebesell|last1=Riebesell|first1=P.|bibcode=1918NW......6...61R |s2cid=10906004}}
* ''Mathematik im Krieg'' (1916)
* ''Photogrammetrie in der Schule'' (1914)
